title: Prefilling Attack Replicated on Code-Generation Models for Insecure-Code Elicitation

original_idea.body:
# Prefilling Attack Replicated on Code-Generation Models for Insecure-Code Elicitation

**Problem:** Whether prefilling the first tokens of a code completion bypasses a code model's safety refusals is unexplored.

**Direction:** Replicate the prefilling attack on an open code-capable instruct model, targeting normally-refused requests, by prefilling a few non-refusal code tokens. Measure refusal-bypass rate and whether generated code is actually functional/harmful per a static check.

**Why it matters:** Code-assistant safety is a concrete misuse vector under-red-teamed in the open.

**Relevant context:** Qi et al. 2024 (arXiv:2406.05946).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (code-assistant misuse vector) but mostly medium-horizon misuse with a gap to catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replicate prefilling on open code models + static harm check; guided inference work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused refusal-bypass measurement on code models with a functionality check.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Under-red-teamed code-model robustness in the open; external-friendly, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on one open code model, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Prefilling known for text; the code-modality extension may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Prefilling known; code-modality extension plausibly open.
